reason: Escaping infrared energy should cool the hot surface, directly advancing the first goal.
expectation: The surface should lose heat and become cooler.

choice.with: Cooler air high above the surface

alternatives.reason: Cooling atmospheric steam may also start the rain pathway.

effect: The cooler rock can retain liquid water, completing the surface-cooling goal; rain remains to be made.
reaction: The contrast between cool rock and nearby lava makes the uneven cooling clear.
reason: Cooler air should help water vapor in the steam-rich atmosphere condense into clouds.

choice.with: Cooler air high above the surface

expectation: The steam should condense into clouds that can produce rain.

effect: The steam has condensed into clouds; rain still needs to reach the ground.
reaction: The distinction between clouds and a surface ocean is useful.
reason: Gravity should pull water from the clouds down as rain.
expectation: Rain should fall from the clouds toward the ground.

effect: Rain is falling, but it may evaporate or boil before accumulating; the cool rock offers a place for it to reach the ground.
reaction: The possibility of rain recycling before it collects is interesting.
reason: The cool rock should allow falling rain to survive on the surface.
expectation: Rain should reach the cool rock and remain liquid.

effect: Rain remained liquid on the cool rock, completing the final goal and showing that water can accumulate despite nearby lava.
reaction: It was satisfying to see the cooling and rain pathways come together.

mostWorthwhile.text: Cooling the surface was most worthwhile: the contrast between rock that retains water and lava that boils it away made uneven cooling concrete.

leastWorthwhile.text: The separate step of making rain fall felt somewhat predictable after forming clouds, although it did clarify that droplets can evaporate before collecting.

surprise.text: I was interested that rain can fall yet recycle through evaporation or boiling instead of accumulating.

arbitrary.text: No action felt particularly arbitrary; each had a clear role in cooling or bringing water to the ground.

continue.text: I would continue: the linked cooling and condensation steps made me curious how the accumulated water develops into a sea.
